title: DC-area forecast: Heat plus storm chances through Friday; nicer by holiday weekend
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Clouds from earlier storms diminish during the evening, with rain-cooled temperatures mainly in the mid-70s to low 80s.

What’s next? Hot and humid tomorrow with highs in the mid-90s, the heat index up to 100 to 105, and a chance for late-day storms. Only slightly cooler Friday with more showers and storms possible, then looking like a pretty nice Labor Day weekend.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: An isolated quick shower possible this evening with skies turning partly cloudy. Muggy evening temperatures in the mid-70s to low 80s dip to overnight lows in the low to mid-70s. There could be another shower or rumble around or after midnight. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): The cool front retreats to the northeast, likely leaving the entire region partly to mostly sunny and hot. Highs should reach the mid-90s with heat indexes rising to around 100 to 105. Scattered strong to severe storms are possible by late afternoon, probably after 3 or 4 p.m. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: After the chance of scattered strong to severe storms into the evening, skies are partly to mostly cloudy overnight with lows in the low to mid-70s and still humid. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Temperatures only come down slightly Friday with highs near 90 to the low 90s. Humidity stays up, and it's one more day with potential for scattered showers and storms as a front lingers nearby. Rain chances may continue into Friday evening but should diminish overnight. Humidity should also start to decline overnight with lows in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Low-Medium

The forecast is an encouraging one for Labor Day weekend. Can't rule out a shower south or west of DC on Saturday. But overall we should be partly to mostly sunny, mostly dry, and less humid Saturday through Monday. Highs in the low to mid-80s Saturday trend a little cooler Sunday and Monday, when highs top out in the upper 70s to mid-80s. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 2

Blistering late-season heat in 1980 sent temperatures to 101 degrees, part of a record-setting stretch of 90-degree days that extended deep into September.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: Not quite as hot as Tuesday, but still steamier than most of us would prefer for early September. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
